title: data: created_at is client-writable on an ordinary PATCH — the audit anchor can be forged silently
body:
Found while verifying the 17.0.0-rc.1 checklist on #3909 (section C, "write observability — `droppedFields`"). Verified on `main` @ `1ee48bc60`, showcase under `os serve --dev`, ordinary admin session (no `isSystem`).

`created_at` accepts a client-supplied value on an ordinary REST write and **persists it**:

```
PATCH /api/v1/data/showcase_task/<id>   {"progress":42,"created_at":"1999-01-01T00:00:00Z"}
→ 200

GET  …?select=created_at,progress   → {"created_at":"1999-01-01T00:00:00.000Z","progress":42}
sqlite> select created_at from showcase_task where id='<id>';
        1999-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
```

Its two siblings are correctly protected — the same request shape aimed at `updated_at` and `created_by` leaves both untouched (`updated_at` keeps the engine's real timestamp, `created_by` stays as it was). So this is one field out of the audit trio, not a general posture.

The field metadata confirms nothing marks it:

```json
"created_at": {"label":"Created At","type":"datetime","readonly":false, …}
```

`readonly: false` on a system-managed audit timestamp is the root of it — the write path has no reason to drop the value, which is also why **no `droppedFields` is reported**: from the platform's point of view nothing was dropped. (Genuinely computed fields are handled elsewhere and correctly: writing `f_formula` / `f_summary` is rejected 400 `INVALID_FIELD` rather than dropped.)

## Why it matters

`created_at` is the anchor of the audit timeline — the field the historical-import work (#3479/#3493) deliberately preserves, the one dashboards bucket on, and the one an auditor reads to establish when a record came into existence. Any authenticated caller who can edit a record can forge it, silently, in the same request that makes a legitimate edit. There is no diagnostic: the response is a normal 200 with the record, and the forged value reads back as truth from then on.

It also leaves the #3794 `droppedFields` contract untestable on the most obvious input a reviewer would reach for. I could not find a path on this build that produces a non-empty `droppedFields` — computed fields 400, unknown fields 400, and system fields (this one) are simply written. Worth confirming the contract has live coverage rather than only the FLS path.

## Expected

`created_at` is engine-owned like `updated_at`: a client-supplied value is dropped (and reported in `droppedFields`, which is exactly the case that key exists for) rather than persisted. If back-dating must remain possible, it belongs behind the historical-import path that already argues for it (`isSystem` / the import wizard's "import as historical data"), not on the ordinary write path.

Part of the #3909 rc.0/rc.1 verification (section C).
